heading: Tac: every service language
body: Tac supports shared role modules in every Tac language: JavaScript, TypeScript, Dart, Swift, Kotlin, Java, C#, F#, Rust, Go, Ruby and Python. The example declares a MoneyEntity mapping in the required client/entities folder. Table is a modifier and does not change that path. The view shows local service state, not the result of a database query. Declaring an entity does not connect to a database and does not fetch data. To run queries, explicitly supply an authorized public client adapter and own its behavior context. Select one language tab and copy its service file and entity file. The shared page client/pages/tac.html places <money-panel hydrate="load" />, and the view reads {money.amount}. Annotation discovery selects that language automatically. The native application opens that page, because the manifest's start_url is /. JavaScript, TypeScript and Dart run on every target. Rust links on macOS, Windows and Linux, C# links on Windows, and both reach every other target, including the web, as WebAssembly. Go reaches every target as WebAssembly (ADR 0035, ADR 0037, ADR 0045). F# runs on the same .NET browser runtime as C# on every target. Java reaches the page as WebAssembly through TeaVM, and Ruby through Tachyon's mruby WebAssembly runtime (ADR 0049). Swift links on macOS and iOS and Kotlin on Android. Both reach every other target as WebAssembly, where the built-in Store keeps its rows in IndexedDB, as it does for the other WebAssembly languages (ADR 0059, ADR 0078, ADR 0082). Keep the native MoneyService type first in the file. The compiler appends the discovered entity declarations after it. Tac stays client-rendered. It uses only public TAC_ configuration, never private Yon credentials. Lua has no tab here, because the build refuses Entity in Lua Tac code with TY1308. A Python entity builds, and its markers are snake_case, such as `@entity`, `@table` and `Annotated[int, id]`. A Python service saves these records through a Store, as the other languages do. Python runs on its pinned runtime in the page on every target (ADR 0093). C++ has no tab here, because the build refuses Entity in C++ Tac code with TY1308 (ADR 0099).
